subject: CAIQ control index and sample artifacts — next steps
messages:
From: Lina Park <lina.park@cardinalhealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-01-12T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: CAIQ intake — initial control list and evidence ask

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for taking this on. Cardinal Health's security assessment team started a CAIQ intake specific to our upcoming vendor review. We need a crosswalk that maps Redwood's CAIQ answers to control identifiers (CSA CCM + carrier control IDs), plus representative artifacts for a handful of controls we flagged as high priority: data residency, key management, runtime isolation, and telemetry retention.

Ask: can you provide a control index (spreadsheet) that includes CAIQ question id, your short answer, control mapping, and a pointer to a sample artifact or log snippet? We would also like one runtime log sample (scrubbed) showing request flow and an HSM/KMS attestation excerpt.

Timeline: Cardinal's intake portal window opens next Wednesday; ideally we have an index and the two sample artifacts by EOD Friday so we can upload and schedule a walkthrough.

Thanks — happy to coordinate a short call if useful.

— Lina
Security Intake Lead, Cardinal Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Lina Park <lina.park@cardinalhealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-12T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: CAIQ intake — initial control list and evidence ask

Hi Lina,

Appreciate the clear list. I've attached a first-pass control index (CAIQ_Control_Index_v1.xlsx) that maps our CAIQ responses to CSA CCM control IDs and includes a short "owner" column so you know who to follow up with internally. High-level notes:

- Data residency: we call out region-level tenancy and our optional private deployment offering; see control rows CCM-SS-03 and CCM-RES-02 for the specific artifacts.
- Key management: KMS attestation snippet included (redacted); full HSM attestation available under NDA—I've noted that in the index.
- Runtime isolation: included sample runtime log (runtime_log_sample_202612.zip) showing per-tenant KV cache segmentation and request routing metadata.
- Telemetry retention: index points to our retention policy doc and an exported retention log sample.

Proposed next steps:
1) We'll upload the two sample artifacts to your secure portal (please confirm the upload link).
2) Internal owners (cc'd Kimberly and Ben) will be available for a 30-minute walkthrough next Tuesday or Wednesday — propose 10:00 AM PT Tue (1/19).
3) If you need the HSM attestation before the call, we can send a redacted PDF under your NDA.

I'll loop in Jonas for any architectural clarifications if needed.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference
Attachment: CAIQ_Control_Index_v1.xlsx (xlsx)
Attachment: runtime_log_sample_202612.zip (zip, scrubbed)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-13T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: Cardinal CAIQ — evidence owners & prep

Team,

Context: Cardinal's security intake (Lina) needs a CAIQ control index and representative artifacts by EOD Friday. I sent them v1 of the spreadsheet and the runtime log sample; we may need to provide a redacted HSM attestation under NDA.

Please action:
- Kimberly: finalize the KMS/HSM excerpt and confirm whether we can share the redacted attestation under our standard NDA language. Reply with link to redacted PDF by Thu EOD.
- Ben: validate the runtime_log_sample_202612.zip scrub — double-check that tenant IDs and IPs are scraped. If good, stage the upload to the Cardinal secure portal (link in Lina's email) Friday morning.
- Jonas: be on standby for the walkthrough; Lina may ask for a short explanation of our runtime isolation model and KV cache segmentation.

Notes on talking points for walkthrough: keep the explanation short and operational—how requests are routed, prefix caching behavior, fallback model variants, and how we maintain tenant isolation on shared runtimes.

Marissa

From: Lina Park <lina.park@cardinalhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: security@cardinalhealth.com
Date: 2027-01-18T15:32:00-08:00
Subject: Re: CAIQ intake — initial control list and evidence ask

Marissa — thanks, this is great. We received the CAIQ_Control_Index_v1.xlsx in the portal and the runtime log sample looks scrubbed appropriately. Kimberly's redacted KMS excerpt also came through and is sufficient for our intake team.

We scheduled the 30-minute walkthrough for Tue 2027-01-19 10:00 AM PT. Our intake reviewer will focus on CCM-RES-02 (data locality), CCM-CR-04 (runtime segregation), and CCM-TR-01 (telemetry retention). Please have Jonas available for the technical portion and Kimberly for the KMS questions.

I'll close the intake window after the session and post any follow-ups in the portal.

Lina
Security Intake Lead, Cardinal Health
